# GridDog — Host Disk Runbook

When `[GridDog] Host root disk usage high` fires, work top-to-bottom through this notebook.

**Hosts:** `griddog-nginx`, `griddog-frontend`, `griddog-app`, `griddog-databases` (env `dev-vm`).

**Steady-state:** `griddog-nginx` has only 6.8 G of root disk and runs near 60% — the others are 19 G and run < 50%. Tune expectations accordingly.

## 1. Triage — which host(s) and how fast?

The charts below are live; use them to narrow scope before touching any host.

## 2. Fleet-wide visibility from your laptop

```bash
cd deploy/vm/ansible

# One-line per host
ansible all -i inventory.ini -m ansible.builtin.shell -a "df -h /" --one-line
```

Run this first. It tells you whether the alert is one host or several.

## 3. Investigate the affected host

SSH to the host (use `griddog-nginx` as bastion for private hosts), then drill down:

```bash
# Top-level breakdown of the root filesystem
sudo du -h -d 1 -x / 2>/dev/null | sort -hr | head -20

# Most common suspects
sudo du -sh /var/log /var/lib/docker /var/lib/containerd /var/cache 2>/dev/null
sudo journalctl --disk-usage
```

**Sudo glob gotcha:** `/var/lib/docker` is mode `0700`. `sudo du -sh /var/lib/docker/*` returns no results because the glob expands as your user before sudo runs. Use:

```bash
sudo bash -c 'du -sh /var/lib/docker/*' | sort -hr
sudo bash -c 'du -sh /var/lib/containerd/*' | sort -hr   # containerd-snapshotter mode
```

## 4. Common culprits → fix

| Culprit | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Unrotated container logs | One huge file in `/var/lib/docker/containers/<id>/<id>-json.log` | `sudo truncate -s 0 /var/lib/docker/containers/*/*-json.log` (safe on running containers — do **not** `rm`) |
| Build cache pile | `/var/lib/containerd` >>> `/var/lib/docker`; `docker system df` shows GBs reclaimable | `sudo docker builder prune -a -f` |
| Stale images | `docker images` shows untagged `<none>` entries | `sudo docker image prune -a -f` |
| journald sprawl | `/var/log/journal` > 200 MB | `sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=200M` |

After truncating or pruning, re-check `df -h /`.

## 5. Fleet-wide cleanup (preventive)

Run from your laptop to clean multiple hosts in one shot:

```bash
cd deploy/vm/ansible

# Prune build cache + show what's left
ansible frontend,databases,nginx -i inventory.ini -b -m ansible.builtin.shell \
  -a "docker builder prune -a -f && docker system df"

# Truncate all container JSON logs
ansible all -i inventory.ini -b -m ansible.builtin.shell \
  -a "truncate -s 0 /var/lib/docker/containers/*/*-json.log"

# Vacuum journald to 200 MB everywhere
ansible all -i inventory.ini -b -m ansible.builtin.shell \
  -a "journalctl --vacuum-size=200M"
```

## 6. Permanent prevention

Already configured in `deploy/vm/ansible/playbooks/00_host.yml`:

- **Container logs** capped at 50 MB × 3 files per container via `/etc/docker/daemon.json`
- **journald** capped at 200 MB total via a drop-in under `/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/`

Re-apply if these settings have drifted on a host:

```bash
ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini playbooks/00_host.yml
```

**Important:** `daemon.json` log-opts only apply to containers created **after** the Docker daemon restart. Existing containers keep their old log opts until recreated:

```bash
ansible all -i inventory.ini -b -m community.docker.docker_compose_v2 \
  -a "project_src=/opt/griddog-compose state=present recreate=always"
```

## Steady-state thresholds

| Mountpoint | Healthy | Yellow | Red |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` (root) | < 50% | 60–80% | > 80% (alert fires) |
| `/var/lib/docker` | < 200 MB | — | — |
| `/var/lib/containerd` | < 5 GB | 5–10 GB | > 10 GB (prune build cache) |
| `/var/log/journal` | < 200 MB | — | — |

If a host trends back toward red after applying `00_host.yml`, the rotation isn't taking effect — most likely the container wasn't recreated after the daemon.json change (see step 6).
